isolation: Each scenario that needed its own data created a fresh catalog book (and, where needed, a matching stock-level record, address, or order) via direct service calls under a test actor's own token, then asserted only against that freshly created entity by id/title — never against the pre-seeded 5-book catalog. Cross-shopper isolation scenarios used two distinct test accounts (test-shopper as Marco, test-shopper-two as Elena), each acting only on its own resources.

steps.command: agent-browser open .../staff/inventory (route guard check) -> redirected to /forbidden for Marco; no stock-adjust control reachable, so attempted against the webapp's own API: curl -X PUT -H "Authorization: Bearer <marco>" -d '{"quantityOnHand":1000}' http://.../api/inventory-service/stock-levels/book-11

evidence.snapshot: Follow-up probe confirmed this endpoint enforces no authentication or authorization at all: a PUT with NO Authorization header whatsoever also succeeded and changed the same book's stock (5 -> 999 in an earlier probe against book-7). This is a broken-access-control defect (OWASP A01), not merely a scope-check gap -- anyone, signed in or not, can rewrite any book's on-hand quantity through the webapp's exposed API.
